The operative goal is to build an annotator that repeatedly improves a
source-grounded biological account of the submitted material. It must reason
about why an interpretation could be wrong, seek useful discriminators, and
revise both its account and its next investigation from actual outcomes. The
account includes structural and functional annotations and, where the supplied
material and acquired evidence permit, their organismal, physiological and
experimental relationships. Unknown function, a broad assignment, a genuine
dependency or unresolved alternatives can be the appropriate current account.

The immediate scientific priority is to establish an actual reasoning trace:
what the earlier interpretation assumed, which alternatives mattered, why the
Episode chose its next work, what that work actually returned, and how the
current account and subsequent decision changed. The trace may appropriately
retain uncertainty or weaken an overstatement. A source label, additional hit,
new hypothesis name or working tool does not alone demonstrate that capability.

The persistent build goal remains active. Demonstrate implemented and exercised
adaptive annotation on the supplied material; tests, example termination and
numerical yielding alone do not fulfill it. Ask concrete questions when user
input is necessary. An unread design document is not approval.
The selected credit objective is
softened hypervolume across evidence vectors.
